code: # format the detections for spOccupancy, with site covariates and a season dimension rat_sp <- model_matrix_input(y_rat, eff, site_covs = elev, seasons = season, output = "spOccupancy") # view station x season x occasion dimensions dim(rat_sp$y) #> [1] 28  3 11  # the number of stations n_station <- nrow(rat_sp$y) # make the occupancy covariates a list, so covariates that change each season can join elevation rat_sp$occ.covs <- as.list(rat_sp$occ.covs) # a station x season matrix of season numbers, for a trend in occupancy (~ season) rat_sp$occ.covs$season <- matrix(1:3, n_station, 3, byrow = TRUE) # add the station x season covariates rat_sp$occ.covs$rain <- rain rat_sp$occ.covs$temp <- temp # the season of every station, season and occasion, for detection rat_sp$det.covs$season <- array(rep(1:3, each = n_station), dim = dim(rat_sp$y)) # number each station, for a random intercept in detection rat_sp$det.covs$station <- seq_len(n_station) # make the chains repeatable set.seed(1) # fit the multi-season model, with a trend across seasons plus altitude and rainfall on occupancy, rat_t <- tPGOcc(occ.formula = ~ scale(altitude_point) + scale(rain) + season,                 # detection changing with effort, as in colext()                 det.formula = ~ scale(effort),                 # and specify the data source and MCMC settings                 data = rat_sp, n.batch = 600, batch.length = 25, n.burn = 5000,                 n.thin = 10, n.chains = 3, verbose = FALSE) # view the results summary(rat_t) #>  #> Call: #> tPGOcc(occ.formula = ~scale(altitude_point) + scale(rain) + season,  #>     det.formula = ~scale(effort), data = rat_sp, n.batch = 600,  #>     batch.length = 25, verbose = FALSE, n.burn = 5000, n.thin = 10,  #>     n.chains = 3) #>  #> Samples per Chain: 15000 #> Burn-in: 5000 #> Thinning Rate: 10 #> Number of Chains: 3 #> Total Posterior Samples: 3000 #> Run Time (min): 0.1065 #>  #> Occurrence (logit scale):  #>                          Mean     SD    2.5%     50%  97.5%   Rhat  ESS #> (Intercept)           -0.3092 0.6164 -1.5272 -0.3057 0.9187 0.9998 3000 #> scale(altitude_point) -0.0717 0.2549 -0.5824 -0.0710 0.4212 1.0037 3000 #> scale(rain)            0.2421 0.2708 -0.2798  0.2435 0.7852 1.0056 3000 #> season                 0.6269 0.3199  0.0115  0.6252 1.2759 1.0008 3000 #>  #> Detection (logit scale):  #>                  Mean     SD    2.5%     50%  97.5%   Rhat  ESS #> (Intercept)   -0.0942 0.0818 -0.2525 -0.0940 0.0661 1.0003 3168 #> scale(effort) -0.0759 0.0810 -0.2395 -0.0771 0.0844 1.0006 3000 # WildObsR provides programmatic access query, download prepare camera trap data WildObs Database. Every project arrives Camera Trap Data Package (Camtrap DP), meaning dataset contains tables camera deployments, wildlife detections media (.e., images /videos), along Creative Commons licences, formatted citations field definitions travel . Discover data exist: search projects place, time, species, sampling design contributor, including embargoed projects, listed data released. Access curated data packages, threatened-species records protected, image records, citation every project (cite_datapackages()). Interoperate Camtrap DP tools: as_camtrapdp() converts canonical Camtrap DP camtrapdp camtrapR packages GBIF. Harmonise projects different designs: group cameras cells size, rebuild long-term deployments, reclassify independent detections. Add spatial context: state, IBRA bioregion CAPAD protected area, layers shipped package. Full documentation tutorials: https://wildobs.github.io/WildObsR/

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Example usage with pre-processed camera trap data, accessed from WildObs:  # Load the general use WildObs API key api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY") # use WildObsR function to access data dp <- WildObsR::wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001") # extract first DP from the list dp <- dp[[1]]  # Extract resources from the data package covs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "covariates") obs  <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations") deps <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")  # Assign spatial scales # 'scales' defines the area (in square meters) covered by the hexagonal cell scales <- c(1000000, 3000000)  # Generate spatial hexagons based on the provided scales covs <- WildObsR::spatial_hexagon_generator(covs, scales)  # Identify matching columns between deployments and covariates cols <- names(deps)[names(deps) %in% names(covs)] # Merge deployment information to the covariates covs <- merge(deps, covs, by = cols)  # Note: This overwrites the original covs data  # Define columns for mode aggregation (example: 'projectName' and 'habitat') mode_cols_covs <- names(covs)[grepl("projectName|habitat", names(covs))] # Set the method for aggregating the total number of individuals detected: individuals <- "sum"  # Alternative: "max" # Specify observation-level covariate variables derived from deployments. # These variables capture information that varies in space and time. obs_covs <- c("baitUse", "featureType", "setupBy", "cameraModel", "cameraDelay","cameraHeight", "cameraDepth", "cameraTilt", "cameraHeading", "detectionDistance", "deploymentTags")  # now spatially resample the data, noting that this function may take a few minutes to run resamp_data = WildObsR::resample_covariates_and_observations(covs, obs, individuals = "sum", mode_cols_covs, obs_covs)  # Select the resampled observations and covs at the 1 km scale resamp_obs = resamp_data$spatially_resampled_observations$cellID_1km resamp_covs = resamp_data$spatially_resampled_covariates$cellID_1km  # Run the matrix generator function res <- matrix_generator(   obs = resamp_obs,   covs = resamp_covs,   dur = 110,   w = 3,   site_covs = c("mode_habitat", "Avg_human_footprint_10km2", "locationName", "Avg_FLII_3km2"),   obs_covs = c("cameraHeight", "featureType", "cameraModel"),   all_locationNames = TRUE,   scientificNames = c("Orthonyx spaldingii", "Uromys caudimaculatus"),   type = "abundance",   individuals = "sum" ) # Access the detection matrix for one species: res[["Orthonyx_spaldingii"]][["detection_matrix"]] } # }

title: Generate spatially distinct sampling units — spatial_hexagon_generator
code: # Create example camera-trap metadata # \donttest{ set.seed(42)  # Simulate 12 camera deployments across 3 sites and 2 contributors data <- tibble::tibble(   deploymentID = paste0("cam_", 1:12),   locationName = rep(c("Site_A", "Site_B", "Site_C"), each = 4),   projectName = rep(c("UQ_team", "CSIRO_team"), length.out = 12),    # Cluster each site around distinct centers (approx Wet Tropics, QLD)   latitude = c(     rnorm(4, mean = -17.10, sd = 0.01),   # Site_A: tight cluster     rnorm(4, mean = -17.25, sd = 0.005),  # Site_B: tighter cluster     rnorm(4, mean = -16.95, sd = 0.03)    # Site_C: more spread out   ),   longitude = c(     rnorm(4, mean = 145.65, sd = 0.01),   # Site_A     rnorm(4, mean = 145.50, sd = 0.005),  # Site_B     rnorm(4, mean = 145.75, sd = 0.03)    # Site_C   ),    # Random deployment dates over two months   deploymentStart = as.POSIXct("2023-07-01") + runif(12, 0, 30) * 86400,   deploymentEnd   = as.POSIXct("2023-09-01") + runif(12, 0, 30) * 86400 )  # Simulate a column that identifies unique survey events data$deploymentGroups <- paste0(data$locationName, "_", format(data$deploymentStart, "%Y"))  # --- Define grid scales --- # The values represent hexagon *areas* in square meters. # 1e6 = 1 km² hexagons; 25e6 = 25 km² hexagons. scales <- c(1e6, 25e6)  # --- Generate hexagonal sampling units --- hex_data <- spatial_hexagon_generator(data, scales) #> Warning: spatial_hexagon_generator() found cells that several projects sampled at overlapping times: #>   polygon_25km2: 2 cell(s), e.g. Site_A_2_cellID_25km2, Site_B_2_cellID_25km2; projects CSIRO_team, UQ_team #> Each project keeps its own cellID, so their detections and effort stay separate. To inspect them, filter the result on those polygon values; to model them as one site, give the deployments a shared cellID before building the effort matrix.  # Inspect new columns (polygon_ and cellID_ per scale) dplyr::select(hex_data, deploymentID, starts_with("polygon"), starts_with("cellID")) %>%   head() #>   deploymentID          polygon_1km2         polygon_25km2 #> 1        cam_1  Site_A_4_cellID_1km2 Site_A_2_cellID_25km2 #> 2        cam_2  Site_A_7_cellID_1km2 Site_A_2_cellID_25km2 #> 3        cam_3  Site_A_9_cellID_1km2 Site_A_2_cellID_25km2 #> 4        cam_4 Site_A_12_cellID_1km2 Site_A_2_cellID_25km2 #> 5        cam_5  Site_B_4_cellID_1km2 Site_B_2_cellID_25km2 #> 6        cam_6  Site_B_2_cellID_1km2 Site_B_2_cellID_25km2 #>                             cellID_1km2                          cellID_25km2 #> 1     Site_A_4_cellID_1km2_2023_UQ_team    Site_A_2_cellID_25km2_2023_UQ_team #> 2  Site_A_7_cellID_1km2_2023_CSIRO_team Site_A_2_cellID_25km2_2023_CSIRO_team #> 3     Site_A_9_cellID_1km2_2023_UQ_team    Site_A_2_cellID_25km2_2023_UQ_team #> 4 Site_A_12_cellID_1km2_2023_CSIRO_team Site_A_2_cellID_25km2_2023_CSIRO_team #> 5     Site_B_4_cellID_1km2_2023_UQ_team    Site_B_2_cellID_25km2_2023_UQ_team #> 6  Site_B_2_cellID_1km2_2023_CSIRO_team Site_B_2_cellID_25km2_2023_CSIRO_team # }

These have now been condensed into one row with the updated deploymentID: Loc1_deployment_1"  # View updated deployments results$deployments #>        deploymentID locationID deploymentStart deploymentEnd deploymentGroups #> 1 Loc1_deployment_1       Loc1      2020-01-01    2020-01-15             <NA>  # Check updated observation and media deployment IDs results$observations #>   observationID      deploymentID locationID #> 1             1 Loc1_deployment_1       Loc1 #> 2             2 Loc1_deployment_1       Loc1 #> 3             3 Loc1_deployment_1       Loc1 #> 4             4 Loc1_deployment_1       Loc1 results$media #>   mediaID      deploymentID #> 1      m1 Loc1_deployment_1 #> 2      m2 Loc1_deployment_1 #> 3      m3 Loc1_deployment_1 #> 4      m4 Loc1_deployment_1
